narrative: Solayer, a Solana-based derivatives platform, claims to be the first venue to list a pearl-2:native perpetual future, adding a new (and verified-live) trading venue to the ecosystem catalog. Yesterday's relay custody fix continues to hold — re-checked independently again, still clean. Network difficulty ticked up for the first time in weeks (22.16M → 22.44M) alongside faster blocks and a mining mix now dominated by Kryptex (52 of the last 100 blocks, up sharply from its usual ~20%) — consistent with the community prediction flagged yesterday about an imminent difficulty spike, though still not officially confirmed. Price recovered +6% after its recent dip. GitHub picked up again: the core repo shipped a testnet2-only fork-ordering fix, and the long-dormant blockbook repo packaged its OpenAPI spec into the runtime image.

incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height (91,737) is past the fork — the fix is live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields are null this snapshot pending a replacement public data source.

The bridge relay's /api/custody endpoint briefly reported a negative surplus (WPRL supply ~28,800 PRL above locked PRL), driven by its lockGrains field reading well below an independent read of the same address. WPRL total supply was independently confirmed correct via a direct Ethereum RPC call to the contract's totalSupply(). prlscan's own ledger for the lock address (received minus sent, self-consistent) put its balance about 38,900 PRL higher than the relay reported, and no single recent transaction in that address's history explains a real shortfall of that size — pointing to a bug or stale field in the relay's custody rollup rather than an actual funding gap. TVL and surplus fields are null in this snapshot pending relay-side confirmation; not treated as a confirmed incident, but flagged here for visibility and follow-up.

The relay custody-data issue from 2026-08-03 is worse, not resolved: /api/custody's lockGrains now reads a flat 0 for the lock address, and the reported deficit widened to roughly -76,300 PRL. Re-verified independently the same way — prlscan's own ledger shows the address holds a real, non-zero, slightly-growing balance (~85,588 PRL), and a fresh Ethereum RPC call confirms /api/supply (not /api/custody's totalSupplyGrains, now separately 848 PRL stale) matches the true on-chain WPRL total exactly. Reconstructing custody from the verified pieces gives a healthy ~+10,141 PRL surplus, in line with the recent trend. This is now a two-day, worsening pattern isolated to the relay's own custody-monitoring integration rather than an actual funding gap — escalated for direct engineering follow-up. TVL/surplus remain null pending a fix and re-verification.

Resolved: the relay custody-data issue tracked on 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-04 is fixed. /api/custody's lockGrains and totalSupplyGrains now match independent verification exactly — prlscan's lock-address ledger and a direct Ethereum RPC totalSupply() call both agree with the relay byte-for-byte. Surplus reads a healthy +10,178.73 PRL (1.03%), almost exactly matching this dashboard's own reconstruction of the true figure during the two-day episode. TVL/surplus fields are populated normally again this run. At no point during the episode did it appear in public social discussion, consistent with it having been an internal relay-monitoring bug rather than anything user-facing.
